pr_title: Use original filename for extension name check
pr_body:
The loading of an extension image from a symlink "NAME.raw" to
"NAME-VERSION.raw" failed because the release file name check worked
with the backing file of the loop device which already resolves the
symlink and thus the found name "NAME-VERSION" mismatched "NAME".
Pass the original filename and use it instead of the backing file
when available. This fixes the loading of "NAME.raw" extensions which
are a symlink to "NAME-VERSION.raw" as, e.g., may be the case when
systemd-sysupdate manages multiple versions.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/24293
pr_comments:
So I think we should go the other way. i.e. change the rules for finding the extension file in the image. Instead of stupidly using the original filename without suffix, only start with that, and if this results in ENOENT, chop off everything after the final "-" or "_" char and try again. And then do that again. And again. Until no "-" or "_" are in the extension name anymore.

This would mean if you have an image file `foo-bar-baz_47.raw`, then we'd first search for `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.foo-bar-baz_47` in the image. And if that doesn't exist, then we'd search for `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.foo-bar-baz`, and then `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.foo-bar` and then `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.foo`, and fail if that also doesn't exist.

That is more flexible I think, it allows you to add suffixes freely, but still enforces the idea that the name matters to some point at least.

I found it a bit surprising that instead of working with the name of the symlink we work with the name of the final file because that's not what I expect as user.
The suggested alternative is also ok for me, I can have a look next week. (The sysext name would come from the extension release file. If more than one extension with the same name is in a folder, the first wins.)

I agree with your thinking. I guess if there are symlinks involved, we probably should understand them like UNIX usually does in this case, i.e. only look at the symlink name, ignore the target name...

That said, I also agree with my earlier thinking. ;-) i.e. I think if we have an image called "foo-4711.raw" it should also work with only a extension-release.foo file...

So maybe implement both schemes? Yours *and* the one I proposed?

(But I can understand if you only do the one you proposed for now, and leave the other thing for someone else/another time...)

Anyway, needs a rebase now, too

> So maybe implement both schemes? Yours _and_ the one I proposed?

I've just started to look into the suffix topic and without this PR here it would mean that we don't enforce a naming of the entry under the extension directories. One could try to enforce it even for both but I would just care about the names in the extension directories and leave the symlink target name unrestricted.

issue_context.title: sysext image filename check too strict with symlink usage
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

250

### Used distribution

Fedora 36

### Linux kernel version used

_No response_

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

_No response_

### Component

systemd-sysext

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

The setup follows a scheme that is meant to be used with systemd-sysupdate, where more than one version of a sysext image is stored in a folder with a version marker like "NAME-VERSION.raw" and a "NAME-current.raw" symlink is managed by systemd-sysupdate. The final "/etc/extensions/NAME.raw" file is just a symlink to the "NAME-current.raw" symlink which itself is a symylink to "NAME-VERSION.raw".
Both systemd-sysext or systemd-dissect should load the sysext image and only consider the first symlink name for the filename check. This already works for sysext directories.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

Both systemd-sysext and systemd-dissect fail to load the sysext image because they seems to take the backing filename into account instead of the first symlink's name.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create a working myext.raw sysext image (place in /etc/extensions/ and restart `systemd-sysext.service` to verify it works)
2. Now move the myext.raw image to `/tmp/myext-1.raw`
3. Let `/etc/extensions/myext.raw` be a symlink to `/tmp/myext-1.raw`
4. Restart `systemd-sysext.service` and see that it fails with `Failed to read metadata for image myext: No medium found`

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments: The problem comes from retrieving the image file name by looking up the backing file of the loop dev while the other output of `systemd-dissect` uses the name of the symlink. I think it makes sense to pass the name as additional parameter to skip the lookup of the backing file.
